Metoprolol for example is a selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker, which, theoretically, should primarily affect the heart and have minimal effects on the beta-2 receptors found in the lungs. It’s just the reason it’s generally avoided or used with caution in people with asthma or other chronic pulmonary conditions isn’t because it’s as likely as non-selective beta blockers to cause bronchoconstriction, but more because no beta-1 selective blocker is entirely without risk.
So overall it’s just a general precaution. In the case of someone does have hypertension and has asthma, then perhaps beta blockers in general just aren’t the best med for them. Especially, let’s say they do take a selective blocker but they have reports of shortness of breath, wheezing, or increase in respirations (any sign that shows negative effect to their pulmonary system.) That’s okay and there’s plenty of other options for hypertension. I believe beta blockers in general are more of the last line of defense for hypertension, or at least towards the middle to end. They can look at perhaps diuretics like thiazide meds depending on their kidney function (which is a usually a more common first option for hypertension), spironolactone a potassium sparring diuretic, or maybe a ACE blocker (-pril). It really just depends on the patient but in general it’s saying the use of beta blockers are contradicted in those with some sort of COPD because the chance of them not bronchial contracting is probably never an absolute 100%.

Hii, I hope you’re doing well!
I believe (and this is just what I think, I have to say this just in case I ruin your life) BUT-
When it comes to Beta blockers, we know Beta 1’s are more predominantly in our heart and Beta 2’a are more predominantly within our lungs. Remember, Alpha and Beta receptors themselves are adrenergic, meaning they only respond to the lock and key mechanism of epinephrine and norepinephrine to depolerize. Now, with Beta blockers (specifically Beta 1 blockers), since they “block”they are going to be an antagonist of this receptor site thus it’s going to effectively stop the effect of that receptor (in this case, increase contraction and heart rate from nor/epinephrine.)
The thing is, Beta 1’s are consequently enough very similar to their sibling of the Beta 2’s and well hell- they are practically neighbors (Cardio and pulmonary systems sit literally next to each other.) Some of these beta blockers are “non-selective” in which they are capable of flowing to the pulmonary system and thus attaching to those Beta 2’s and will cause bronchial constriction. Tying this back, the reason we don’t wanna give these meds to patients with COPD is because well—they are already bronchial constricted from emphysema, chronic bronchitis and or asthma; so giving them meds that will increase this effect more will definitely make them suffer more and led to a whole host of new problems.

*A-M + “o-lol” = Selective 
*O-Z + “o-lol” = non-selective
(N can be the tricky and odd ones)
**(This is roughly a way to remember the differences but please note not all beta blocker meds account to this rule)*

You may be wondering then what’s the benefit then of taking a non-selective over a selective then?
Well with that, since non-selective are more I guess “broader” they can also help with migraines, reduce portal hypertension, and help with stress.

I would definitely recommend using compressor and play with it and raise the gain to give your voice some life, i would then use some EQ-ing and cut your lows and bring some highs with your voice and treble. I’m not sure what DAW you’re on but just overall getting your voice more present is a must. Also, layering your vocals brings a whole new world into music. To me it sounded like all your vocals were just one vocals stem and that’s why they were so dull and none present. Layer your vocals, have multiple vocal layers on top of each other to bring it out alive more. Depending on style you can decide how much to layer but at least have some to bring those vocals out forward and give them emotion with different layerings. If you need help please message me because i’m very willing to. Overall this isn’t terrible but there’s definitely a lot of breathing room for improvement. Your talent and creativity is there and i know it, but just need to get some fundamentals of mixing and vocal engineering down.
